clue.text: Support Hal's inebriation by violent reaction

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

indicators.note: drunkenness sends the letters of the name staggering into a new order

parts.note: the name Hal with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A drunken Hal provokes a violent backlash from those he relies on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inebriation' is the anagram signal: a drunk Hal reels, and the S of his possessive counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong hostile response against some change or event.

clue.text: French desk for the office

explanation.surface: A French writing desk ends up serving as the office.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the word names a writing desk; in English it also means an agency or department office.

clue.text: Do an offence, and the judge may do this to you

definitions.text: the judge may do this to you

explanation.surface: Break the law and the judge will send you down.
explanation.definitionFit: One perpetrates a crime, and a judge sends a defendant for trial or to prison.

clue.text: The Mediterraneans who shook Stalin

indicators.note: shaking the dictator's name jumbles its letters into another order

explanation.surface: Southern European peoples who rattled the Soviet dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: Latins are the peoples of Romance-speaking southern Europe around that sea.

clue.text: The printed score for a bedtime lullaby?

explanation.surface: Written-out notation for a song to send a child to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads it as music for the bedsheets, a song sung in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed notation of a composition is its paper score; whimsically, songs for between the bedclothes.

clue.text: Maybe a wee nip to nip in the bud

explanation.surface: A small dram of whisky to stop something early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee nip' is a small dram of whisky from Scotland; to scotch a rumour is to crush it.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky from Scotland is drunk in small drams; as a verb it means to stamp out early.

clue.text: Squeeze what should be squeezed before applying to the fevered brow

definitions.text: what should be squeezed before applying to the fevered brow

explanation.surface: Wring out the cloth before laying it on a hot forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means press tightly together; as a noun, a wet pad laid on the skin to cool it.

clue.text: Twist what the lion teaser twists and flee

definitions.text: Twist what the lion teaser twists

explanation.surface: Someone tormenting a lion twists its tail, then runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone teasing a lion twists its tail; the phrase also means to run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, rotate the hindmost appendage; idiomatically, retreat in a hurry.

clue.text: Whereon bills are posted for stashing away

explanation.surface: A board for posters is somewhere to stash things.
explanation.definitionFit: A large billboard displays posters; storing up a secret supply is also called this.

clue.text: Posted off with the sentence wiped out

explanation.surface: Mailed away after the prison term was cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Money sent by post has been sent off; a punishment cancelled has been pardoned.

clue.text: In South Africa my navy finds Turkish port

indicators.note: the first two letters for the country take the other pieces inside them

parts.note: taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor in South Africa discovers a harbour in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Smyrna is the old name of Izmir.
explanation.definitionFit: Smyrna was the historic Aegean harbour city now called Izmir.

clue.text: Foreigner satisfied his appetite to offend

parts.note: an alien is a person from another country
a man who has eaten has satisfied his hunger

explanation.surface: An outsider ate his fill, causing offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange or antagonise someone is to make them hostile.

clue.text: Traced in order to be put in the box

indicators.note: putting the letters of the word into a new order

explanation.surface: Something was tracked down so that it could be boxed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods packed into a wooden case for shipping have been boxed.

clue.text: Excessive claim made by centre party politician

definitions.text: claim made by centre party politician

explanation.surface: A centrist's statement about themselves sounds overblown.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into I'M MODERATE, what a centrist might claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Going beyond reasonable limits is excessive; split, it is a centrist's self-description.

clue.text: Surrender achieved by assignment given to Polaris?

explanation.surface: Giving in after being assigned to a missile boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Polaris was a nuclear missile carried by submarines, so its assignment is a SUB MISSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding to another is submitting; split, it is a task for a submarine.

clue.text: The artful chiseller

parts.note: a chiseller is a cheat, but here it is someone wielding a chisel in the arts

explanation.surface: A crafty swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chiseller' suggests a cheat and 'artful' cunning; it is an artist who carves stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A carver of statues works with a chisel as an artist.

clue.text: Officially seizes one thousand quid

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
quid is British slang for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: The authorities confiscate a thousand-and-one pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Confiscating property by legal right is to seize it.

clue.text: Single note not up to the quality of hi-fi stereo?

definitions.text: not up to the quality of hi-fi stereo?

explanation.surface: A one-note sound falls short of stereo quality.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as MONO TONE, a single-channel sound poorer than stereo.
explanation.definitionFit: An unvarying pitch is a single note; split, it is single-channel sound.

clue.text: He sets up organic manure incorporating one or more

indicators.note: more signals a further piece added at the end
the manure takes the next piece inside itself

parts.note: compost is rotted organic matter used as manure
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener prepares manure with an extra ingredient or two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He sets up' means sets type: a compositor arranges type for printing.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter in printing sets up the type for pages.

clue.text: Maybe an air-raid shelter for an air-raid official

explanation.surface: A wartime shelter for the man in charge during raids.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as WAR DEN, a hideaway in wartime; an ARP warden policed the blackout in WWII Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, a hideaway in wartime; whole, a civil-defence officer during bombing raids.

clue.text: The pharaoh who got an ambassador surrounded by police

indicators.note: the police word goes round the other piece

parts.note: cops are police officers
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An Egyptian king saw his envoy encircled by officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheops, or Khufu, was the Egyptian king who built the Great Pyramid.

clue.text: Brother Livingstone gone to pieces

parts.note: Ken Livingstone is a British politician, former Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A sibling of Livingstone has fallen apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shattered is in fragments.

clue.text: Just observe what fortune tellers do

explanation.surface: Fortune tellers merely watch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads it as looking ahead into what lies on.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators simply watch; seers gaze forward into the future.

clue.text: Homer apt to produce a figure of speech

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: The Greek poet was well placed to create rhetorical imagery.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a thing as if it were another is a rhetorical device.

clue.text: Five sixths of a shilling added for a bit more muscle

parts.note: a shilling was twelve old pence, so five sixths is ten pence, written 10d
on means in addition, as in 'and so on'

explanation.surface: Paying an extra ten pence to bulk up.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was an old British coin worth twelve pence, d being the old penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The cord joining muscle to bone is an extension beyond the fleshy part.

clue.text: A really good gander displays a tough appearance

explanation.surface: A proper look at something reveals a stern expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gander' is British slang for a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful inspection is a long stare; a stern expression is a severe look.

clue.text: Surest design for peasant dress

indicators.note: designing the word remakes its letters in a new pattern

explanation.surface: A reliable pattern for a country costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet was a coarse reddish homespun cloth worn by country folk.

clue.text: Poet X goes to New York with a child

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A poet goes to America with a child.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate who wrote verse such as In Memoriam.
